To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Resilience and adaptive capacities can be understood as two interrelated concepts that are both process and outcome oriented.

the resilience and adaptive capacities of a livelihood system are a product of its ability to absorb, adapt and transform, in the face of adversity, in ways that are consistent with its underlying values.
resilience is a property of a system that allows it to absorb disturbance without changing the system’s function, and adaptive capacity is the ability of a system to adapt to changing conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how livelihood resilience and adaptive capacity can contribute to a more comprehensive and integrated understanding of livelihoods in the face of adversity, and how these concepts can contribute to the development of more effective interventions.
the conceptualisation of the resilience and the adaptive capacity concepts in relation to livelihoods and the integration of these concepts into livelihoods theory and policy.
the following questions: (1) How can we define resilience and adaptive capacity in the context of livelihoods?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

resilience and adaptive capacity should be considered in the context of the livelihoods framework as an integral component of the livelihoods asset base and as a process of livelihoods transformation.
resilience and adaptive capacity are two distinct, yet interlinked concepts, which are complementary and can be integrated into livelihoods theory and praxis.

resilience is the ability of a system to absorb disturbances and still retain its function, structure and feedbacks, and that adaptive capacity is the ability of the system to change and reorganise while undergoing a perturbation so as to maintain its function, structure, identity and feedbacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the livelihoods approach is a useful conceptual framework for the integration of resilience and adaptive capacity into livelihoods analysis.

the livelihoods resilience and adaptive capacity construct is a complex concept that is not only about the ability to absorb shocks and stressors, or the ability to adapt to change, but rather about the ability of a system (or a livelihood) to maintain or regain its function and structure in the face of disturbances.

the resilience and adaptive capacities of a livelihood are a function of the ability of the system to absorb, adapt and recover from shocks and stresses, as well as the capacity to transform itself to a better state, and to do so within a given time frame.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the concepts of resilience and adaptive capacity are not new in the context of livelihoods, but have been used in different contexts and in different ways, and that there is need to bring together the different strands of thinking in order to build a coherent and useful framework for the study and analysis of the resilience and adaptability of livelihoods.
resilience and adaptive capacity are not only important for livelihoods analysis, but also for the development of livelihoods interventions.

a livelihoods resilience and adaptive capacity framework is not only useful to understand and analyse livelihoods responses to shocks and stresses, but can also be used to design and evaluate livelihoods interventions that seek to enhance the adaptive capacity of communities and individuals to respond to future shocks and stresses.
